title: Gordon Surface
tagline: One B-spline face through a whole network of crossing curves -- every U curve and every V curve, interior ones included.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: A loft passes through one family of sections; a boundary surface only through its edges. Gordon Surface passes through a full U x V network, so interior curves shape the face exactly where you drew them.
useWhen: The shape is defined by curves in both directions
Interior curves must lie on the surface
One smooth face instead of patches
slides.caption: Gordon Surface 1: one face through 5 U and 3 V curves.

points.head: Two skins
points.body: S_u through the U curves (misses V); S_v through the V curves (misses U).

points.head: Minus the grid
points.body: T passes through the crossings only; along each curve it cancels the other skin.

points.head: Exact on both
points.body: The sum reproduces every curve; done control point by control point once compatible.

points.head: Same degree
points.body: Every curve raised to the highest degree -- exactly.

points.head: Same knots
points.body: The union of all interior knots inserted into every curve -- exactly.

points.head: Then blend
points.body: Corresponding control points can be combined; the shapes do not change.

slides.title: The dialog
params: Up to 10 edges, in section order (the pick order is used).
Create S_u / S_v / tensor sheets, show curves (on), print, degree in u and v (3).

items.head: Seed with Interior curves
items.body: Four boundaries -> interior curves that are guaranteed to cross.

items.head: Curves must cross
items.body: Every U must cross every V, in order; a near miss is used silently (midpoint of the closest points).

items.head: Averaged crossings
items.body: Uneven crossing parameters make the fit approximate; arcs' weights are ignored.
